text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. The server often responds with data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access most APIs, you need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove your identity. Be aware of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, since network problems or invalid requests can happen at any time.
